pipeline.title: Fetch assemblies & taxonomy
pipeline.description: Stream NCBI GenBank eukaryote genome summaries via the datasets CLI, extract BioSample coordinates and geo_loc_name, and resolve each assembly to a species-level taxid.

pipeline.title: Build the taxonomic tree
pipeline.description: Walk ENA taxonomy lineages up to Eukaryota for every species with assemblies, then roll up counts for kingdom → genus filters on the map.

pipeline.title: Resolve institute geography
pipeline.description: Match each unique assembly_submitter string to a Research Organization Registry (ROR) record — affiliation chosen-match first, exact query fallback — and attach country plus coordinates.

pipeline.title: Assemble species flows
pipeline.description: Join assemblies, taxonomy, and institutes into one row per species (prefer latest coordinate-bearing assembly, else country-only; human and lab mouse excluded) and write the map parquet.

offshore.definitionNote: Offshore = collection country ISO3 differs from submitter institute country ISO3, among species with both endpoints resolved.

disclaimers.text: High counts for a few institutes — notably Wellcome Sanger Institute (4,842 species, ~26.0% of resolved arcs) — can reflect stricter control over sample and assembly metadata rather than exclusive sequencing capacity. Incomplete geo metadata elsewhere will under-count other labs.

Only 24,346 of 30,613 species with GenBank assemblies (79.5%) carry some retrievable geography (country and/or coordinates). Many species never enter the atlas, so visible flows are a biased slice of real sequencing geography.

geo_loc_name is sample collection locality, not always wild origin. Submitter country (via ROR) is a proxy for where the assembly was deposited — not necessarily where sequencing was performed. Data sourced from INSDC / NCBI GenBank eukaryote assemblies and ROR.
